sections.heading: What is the Two Heaps Pattern?
sections.content: The Two Heaps pattern splits a collection into two halves and keeps each half in a heap. A max heap holds the smaller half, so its top is the largest of the small numbers. A min heap holds the larger half, so its top is the smallest of the large numbers. The two tops sit right at the middle of the data, which gives you the median or any middle-based answer in O(1), with O(log n) per insertion.

sections.heading: When to Use It
items: Find the median of a data stream or sliding window
Find the median of two sorted arrays or a dynamic set
Schedule problems that need both the cheapest and the largest option (IPO, project selection)
Balance two groups where you need the largest of one and the smallest of the other
Any problem that says 'running median', 'middle', 'split into two halves'
Sliding window median or sliding window with a balancing condition
Keywords: median, stream, balance, two halves, capital and profit, IPO

sections.heading: The Intuition
sections.content: Sort all numbers and cut the list in the middle. Everything left of the cut is smaller than everything right of the cut. You only care about the biggest number on the left and the smallest number on the right, because those are the two items next to the middle. A max heap gives you the biggest of the left half instantly, and a min heap gives you the smallest of the right half instantly. Keep the halves equal in size (or the left half one bigger) and the median is always at the tops.

Overflow Warning When Averaging
sections.content: If values can be near Int.MAX_VALUE, small.peek() + large.peek() can overflow. Convert to Long or Double before adding, for example small.peek().toDouble() / 2 + large.peek().toDouble() / 2, or use small.peek().toLong() + large.peek().

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
items: Using two min heaps or two max heaps instead of one of each
Letting the heap sizes drift apart by more than one
Not rebalancing after every insertion
Reading the median from the wrong heap when the count is odd
Integer overflow when adding the two tops for an even count
Calling peek() on an empty heap (peek returns null)
Using PriorityQueue.remove(x) in a sliding window without noting it costs O(k)
Breaking the invariant that every number in the max heap is <= every number in the min heap

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
items: Use a max heap for the smaller half and a min heap for the larger half
Keep their sizes equal, or let the max heap hold one extra element
The median is at the top of one heap or between the two tops
Each insertion costs O(log n), and reading the median costs O(1)
Two heaps also solve scheduling problems where you need the cheapest unlock and the best reward
For sliding windows with removals, consider lazy deletion or a sorted structure
